# Each hash is the sha256 of one of the kit's own Next.js JS chunk bodies
# (originals preserved in kit-source/raw_bodies/, per SHA256SUMS.txt), queried
# live via urlscan's `hash:<sha256>` search. This REPLACES the two dead
# page.url fingerprints (`/api/ws/stripe/sync`, `/static/cg.png`) that never
# matched anything — page.url only ever holds the top-level navigated URL,
# never a WebSocket path or a static asset reference. Content-hash search has
# no such blind spot and, verified live, recovers 60-72 distinct Operator-A
# apexes per hash query (the old page.url fingerprints recovered ~2).
#
# These three seed hashes are from the June-July 2026 kit build (last live
# hit 2026-07-17/07-20 at seed time) — they are the highest-value HISTORICAL
# recovery signal (see docs/indicators.csv for the recovered apex list) but
# will go stale as the operators rebuild the bundle. check.sh's hash-chaining
# step (URLSCAN_KEY required) is what keeps this file current: every fresh
# kit-confirmed scan is fetched via the result API, its chunk hashes are
# extracted, and a new hash is auto-added here once it co-occurs with >=2
# already-known kit apexes.
#
# status: seed = from the original raw_bodies capture; chained = auto-added
# by hash-chaining; candidate = co-occurred with <2 apexes, needs manual
# review before trusting (edit status to "seed"/"chained" once confirmed).
